sanskrit: āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ
english: Foods that promote length of life, vitality, strength, health, ease, and delight, that are savory, smooth, substantial, and gladdening to the heart — such are dear to those of sāttvika nature.

sanskrit: kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ
english: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, exceedingly hot, pungent, harsh, and burning are sought by the man of rajas; they bring pain, sorrow, and disease.

sanskrit: yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat ucchiṣṭam api cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam
english: Food that is stale, drained of its savor, putrid, kept overnight, the leavings of others, and unfit for offering — such is dear to the man of tamas.

sanskrit: aphalākāṅkṣibhir yajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate yaṣṭavyam eveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ
english: That sacrifice which is offered according to the ordinance by those who crave no fruit, the mind being settled in the thought 'this is to be sacrificed and nothing more' — that sacrifice is sāttvika.

sanskrit: abhisaṃdhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārtham api caiva yat ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam
english: But that sacrifice which is offered with an eye to its fruit, and likewise for the sake of display — know that sacrifice, O best of the Bharatas, to be rājasa.

sanskrit: vidhihīnam asṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnam adakṣiṇam śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate
english: A sacrifice devoid of ordinance, with no food distributed, lacking the sacred verses, without priestly gifts, and destitute of faith — that they declare to be tāmasa.

sanskrit: devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucam ārjavam brahmacaryam ahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate
english: Reverence shown to the gods, the twice-born, teachers, and the wise; purity, uprightness, continence, and non-injury — this is called austerity of the body.

sanskrit: anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate
english: Speech that causes no agitation, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, together with the constant practice of sacred recitation — this is called austerity of speech.

sanskrit: manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunam ātmavinigrahaḥ bhāvasaṃśuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam ucyate
english: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity of disposition — this is called austerity of the mind.

sanskrit: śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapas tat trividhaṃ naraiḥ aphalākāṅkṣibhir yuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate
english: This threefold austerity, practiced with the highest faith by disciplined men who crave no fruit, is declared to be sāttvika.

sanskrit: satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat kriyate tad iha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calam adhruvam
english: That austerity which is performed for the sake of respect, honor, and reverence, and out of ostentation, is here declared rājasa — unsteady and impermanent.

sanskrit: mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
english: That austerity which is performed through a deluded notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of ruining another, is declared to be tāmasa.

sanskrit: dātavyam iti yad dānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe deśe kāle ca pātre ca tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam
english: That gift which is given with the thought 'it ought to be given,' to one who can make no return, in a fit place and time and to a worthy recipient — that gift is held to be sāttvika.

sanskrit: yat tu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalam uddiśya vā punaḥ dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ tad dānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam
english: But that gift which is given for the sake of a return, or with an eye to its fruit, or grudgingly — that gift is held to be rājasa.

sanskrit: adeśakāle yad dānam apātrebhyaś ca dīyate asatkṛtam avajñātaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
english: That gift which is given in the wrong place and time and to unworthy persons, without due respect and with contempt, is declared to be tāmasa.

sanskrit: oṃ tat sad iti nirdeśo brahmaṇas trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ brāhmaṇās tena vedāś ca yajñāś ca vihitāḥ purā
english: 'Oṃ Tat Sat' — this is held to be the threefold designation of Brahman; by it of old were ordained the brāhmaṇas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices.

sanskrit: tasmād om ity udāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām
english: Therefore, with the utterance of 'Oṃ,' the acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity prescribed by ordinance ever proceed among those who expound Brahman.

sanskrit: tad ity anabhisaṃdhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ dānakriyāś ca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ
english: With the word 'Tat,' and without aiming at any fruit, the various acts of sacrifice and austerity and the acts of giving are performed by those who seek release (mokṣa).

sanskrit: sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sad ity etat prayujyate praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate
english: In the sense of 'reality' and of 'goodness' the word 'Sat' is employed; and likewise, O Pārtha, the word 'Sat' is applied to an auspicious deed.

sanskrit: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ sad iti cocyate karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sad ity evābhidhīyate
english: Steadfastness in sacrifice, in austerity, and in giving is called 'Sat'; and an action done for the sake of That is likewise designated 'Sat.'

sanskrit: aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapas taptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat asad ity ucyate pārtha na ca tat pretya no iha
english: Whatever is offered, given, or undertaken as austerity, and whatever is done without faith, is called 'Asat,' O Pārtha; it avails nothing hereafter, nor here.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvam icchāmi veditum tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśiniṣūdana
english: Arjuna said: I wish to know, O mighty-armed one, the truth of renunciation (saṃnyāsa) and likewise, distinctly, of relinquishment (tyāga), O Hṛṣīkeśa, O slayer of Keśin.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhus tyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: The seers understand by renunciation the laying aside of acts done from desire; the discerning declare the relinquishment of the fruit of all actions to be relinquishment.

sanskrit: tyājyaṃ doṣavad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyam iti cāpare
english: Some thoughtful men declare that action is to be relinquished as a thing of evil; others, that acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity are not to be relinquished.

sanskrit: niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ
english: Hear my conclusion on this matter of relinquishment, O best of the Bharatas; for relinquishment, O tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.

sanskrit: yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryam eva tat yajño dānaṃ tapaś caiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām
english: Acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity are not to be relinquished; they must indeed be performed. Sacrifice, gift, and austerity are purifiers of the thoughtful.

sanskrit: etāny api tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matam uttamam
english: Yet even these actions are to be performed having abandoned attachment and their fruits — this, O Pārtha, is my settled and supreme conviction.

sanskrit: niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate mohāt tasya parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
english: But the renunciation of a prescribed action is not fitting; its abandonment through delusion is declared to be tāmasa.

sanskrit: duḥkham ity eva yat karma kāyakleśabhayāt tyajet sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet
english: He who relinquishes an action merely because it is painful, from fear of bodily affliction, makes a rājasa relinquishment, and gains none of the fruit of relinquishment.

sanskrit: kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṃ kriyate 'rjuna saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
english: When a prescribed action is performed simply because it ought to be done, O Arjuna, having abandoned attachment and the fruit as well — that relinquishment is held to be sāttvika.

sanskrit: na dveṣṭy akuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ
english: He does not loathe disagreeable work, nor cling to agreeable work — the relinquisher, suffused with sattva, wise, and his doubts cut away.

sanskrit: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ yas tu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate
english: For it is not possible for an embodied being to relinquish actions entirely; but he who relinquishes the fruit of action is called a relinquisher.

sanskrit: aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam bhavaty atyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kva cit
english: The fruit of action is of three kinds — unwished, wished, and mixed — and it accrues after death to those who have not relinquished, but never to the renouncers.

sanskrit: pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me sāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām
english: Learn from me, O mighty-armed one, these five causes, declared in the Sāṃkhya doctrine that brings actions to their end, for the accomplishment of all works.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham vividhāś ca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam
english: The seat of action, likewise the agent, and the instruments of various kinds, the manifold and distinct exertions, and divine providence as the fifth among them.

sanskrit: śarīravāṅmanobhir yat karma prārabhate naraḥ nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ
english: Whatever action a man undertakes with body, speech, or mind, be it right or wrong, these five are its causes.

sanskrit: tatraivaṃ sati kartāram ātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ paśyaty akṛtabuddhitvān na sa paśyati durmatiḥ
english: This being so, he who, through an untrained understanding, looks upon the self alone as the agent — that man of perverse mind does not truly see.

sanskrit: yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate hatvāpi sa imāṃl lokān na hanti na nibadhyate
english: He whose disposition is free of the sense of 'I,' whose understanding is not stained — even though he slay these worlds, he slays not, nor is he bound.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ
english: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower — this is the threefold impulse to action; the instrument, the act, and the agent — this is the threefold sum of action.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvac chṛṇu tāny api
english: Knowledge, action, and the agent are each declared to be of three kinds according to the distinction of the guṇas; hear of these too, duly, in the enumeration of the qualities.

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvam avyayam īkṣate avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu taj jñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam
english: That knowledge by which one beholds in all beings a single, imperishable Being, undivided amid the divided — know that knowledge to be sāttvika.

sanskrit: pṛthaktvena tu yaj jñānaṃ nānābhāvān pṛthagvidhān vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu taj jñānaṃ viddhi rājasam
english: But that knowledge which, by reason of separateness, perceives in all beings manifold existences of distinct kinds — know that knowledge to be rājasa.

sanskrit: yat tu kṛtsnavad ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam atattvārthavad alpaṃ ca tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
english: But that which clings to a single effect as though it were the whole, without reason, having no grasp of the real, and trifling — that is declared to be tāmasa.

sanskrit: niyataṃ saṅgarahitam arāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam aphalaprepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam ucyate
english: An action that is prescribed, free of attachment, done without passion or aversion by one who seeks no fruit — that is called sāttvika.

sanskrit: yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṃkāreṇa vā punaḥ kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tad rājasam udāhṛtam
english: But that action which is performed by one seeking to gratify desire, or again with the sense of 'I,' and with great toil — that is declared to be rājasa.

sanskrit: anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsām anapekṣya ca pauruṣam mohād ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam ucyate
english: That action which is undertaken through delusion, with no regard for its consequence, for loss, for injury, or for one's own capacity — that is called tāmasa.

sanskrit: muktasaṅgo 'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ siddhyasiddhyor nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate
english: Free from attachment, not speaking of himself, endowed with steadfastness and zeal, unmoved in success and failure — such an agent is called sāttvika.

sanskrit: rāgī karmaphalaprepsur lubdho hiṃsātmako 'śuciḥ harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
english: Passionate, eager for the fruit of action, greedy, of a violent nature, impure, swayed by joy and grief — such an agent is declared to be rājasa.

sanskrit: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naikṛtiko 'lasaḥ viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate
english: Undisciplined, vulgar, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, slothful, despondent, and procrastinating — such an agent is called tāmasa.

sanskrit: buddher bhedaṃ dhṛteś caiva guṇatas trividhaṃ śṛṇu procyamānam aśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya
english: Hear now, O Dhanaṃjaya, the threefold distinction of understanding and of steadfastness according to the guṇas, set forth fully and severally.

sanskrit: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
english: That understanding which knows action and abstention, what is to be done and what is not, fear and fearlessness, bondage and release — that, O Pārtha, is sāttvika.

sanskrit: yayā dharmam adharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryam eva ca ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
english: That understanding by which one discerns wrongly right and wrong, and what is to be done and what is not — that understanding, O Pārtha, is rājasa.

sanskrit: adharmaṃ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā sarvārthān viparītāṃś ca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
english: That understanding which, enveloped in darkness, deems wrong to be right and sees all things reversed — that, O Pārtha, is tāmasa.

sanskrit: dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
english: That steadfastness by which, through unwavering yoga, one holds fast the workings of the mind, the breaths, and the senses — that, O Pārtha, is sāttvika.

sanskrit: yayā tu dharmakāmārthān dhṛtyā dhārayate 'rjuna prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
english: But that steadfastness by which, O Arjuna, one clings to duty, pleasure, and wealth, craving their fruit with attachment — that, O Pārtha, is rājasa.

sanskrit: yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madam eva ca na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
english: That steadfastness by which a dull-witted man does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency, and conceit — that, O Pārtha, is tāmasa.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ tv idānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha abhyāsād ramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati
english: Now hear from me, O bull of the Bharatas, of the threefold happiness — that in which one delights through practice and comes to the end of sorrow.

sanskrit: yat tadagre viṣam iva pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam tat sukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktam ātmabuddhiprasādajam
english: That which at first is like poison but in its ripening is like nectar — that happiness, born of the serenity of one's own understanding of the self, is declared sāttvika.

sanskrit: viṣayendriyasaṃyogād yat tadagre 'mṛtopamam pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam
english: That which, born of the contact of the senses with their objects, is at first like nectar but in its ripening is like poison — that happiness is held to be rājasa.

sanskrit: yad agre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanam ātmanaḥ nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
english: That happiness which both at first and in its sequel deludes the self, arising from sleep, sloth, and heedlessness — that is declared to be tāmasa.

sanskrit: na tad asti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ sattvaṃ prakṛtijair muktaṃ yad ebhiḥ syāt tribhir guṇaiḥ
english: There is no being on earth, nor again in heaven among the gods, that could be free from these three guṇas born of Prakṛti.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavair guṇaiḥ
english: The duties of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, and of śūdras too, O scorcher of foes, are apportioned according to the guṇas that spring from their own nature.

sanskrit: śamo damas tapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntir ārjavam eva ca jñānaṃ vijñānam āstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam
english: Calm, self-control, austerity, purity, forbearance, and uprightness, knowledge, discernment, and faith in what is — these are the duties of the brāhmaṇa, born of his own nature.

sanskrit: śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam dānam īśvarabhāvaś ca kṣatrakarma svabhāvajam
english: Heroism, majesty, steadfastness, skill, and not fleeing in battle, generosity, and a lordly bearing — these are the duties of the kṣatriya, born of his own nature.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam
english: Tillage, the tending of cattle, and trade are the duties of the vaiśya, born of his own nature; and the śūdra's duty, born of his nature too, consists of service.

sanskrit: sve sve karmaṇy abhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tac chṛṇu
english: Devoted each to his own duty, a man attains perfection. Hear now how one intent on his own work finds that perfection.

sanskrit: yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam svakarmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ
english: That One from whom the activity of all beings springs, by whom all this is pervaded — worshiping Him through his own work, a man finds perfection.

sanskrit: śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam
english: Better one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Performing the work ordained by one's own nature, a man incurs no guilt.

sanskrit: sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣam api na tyajet sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛtāḥ
english: One should not abandon, O son of Kuntī, the work to which one is born, even though it be flawed; for all undertakings are veiled by flaw, as fire by smoke.

sanskrit: asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati
english: He whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered himself and from whom longing has departed, attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of actionlessness.

sanskrit: siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā
english: Learn from me in brief, O son of Kuntī, how, having attained perfection, one reaches Brahman — that which is the highest consummation of knowledge.

sanskrit: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca śabdādīn viṣayāṃs tyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca
english: Endowed with a purified understanding, restraining the self with steadfastness, abandoning the objects of sense beginning with sound, and casting away passion and aversion;

sanskrit: viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ
english: frequenting solitude, eating but little, with speech, body, and mind controlled, ever devoted to the yoga of meditation, taking refuge in dispassion;

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: having let go of egoism, force, arrogance, desire, anger, and possession, free from the sense of 'mine' and at peace — he becomes fit for oneness with Brahman.

sanskrit: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām
english: Become Brahman, serene in self, he neither grieves nor craves; alike toward all beings, he gains supreme devotion to Me.

sanskrit: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram
english: Through devotion he comes to know Me — how great I am and who I am in truth; then, having known Me in truth, he enters into Me forthwith.

sanskrit: sarvakarmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ matprasādād avāpnoti śāśvataṃ padam avyayam
english: Though ever performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, he attains by My grace the eternal, imperishable abode.

sanskrit: cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ buddhiyogam upāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava
english: Renouncing in thought all actions unto Me, intent on Me, having recourse to the yoga of understanding, be ever fixed in thought upon Me.

sanskrit: maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāt tariṣyasi atha cet tvam ahaṃkārān na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi
english: With your thought on Me, by My grace you shall cross over all difficulties; but if from egoism you will not heed, you shall perish.

sanskrit: yad ahaṃkāram āśritya na yotsya iti manyase mithyaiṣa vyavasāyas te prakṛtis tvāṃ niyokṣyati
english: If, clinging to egoism, you think 'I will not fight,' vain is this resolve of yours; your own nature will compel you.
